question: When setting out a traditional cut roof with an unequal pitch, which trigonometric function is primarily used to calculate the true length of the hip rafter?
options: Sine rule applied to the plan length and pitch angle
Cosine of the roof pitch angle multiplied by the span
Square root of the sum of the squared half-span and squared ridge height
Tangent of the dihedral angle between the hip and common rafter planes

question: In joinery, the term 'diminished stile' refers to which specific feature of a panelled door?
options: A stile that tapers in width toward the bottom rail to allow for a wider bottom panel
A stile that is reduced in thickness to accommodate a planted moulding
A stile that is narrower above the middle rail than below it, typically to accommodate a large bottom panel or glass
A stile that has been reduced in height during installation

question: When calculating the backing bevel for a hip rafter on a square plan roof, which measurement is essential in addition to the roof pitch angle?
options: The length of the common rafter
The dihedral angle between the hip rafter and the roof surface
The angle in plan between the hip rafter and the wall plate
The height of the ridge above the wall plate

question: Which type of wood joint is most appropriate for connecting the corner posts of a heavy timber frame where tensile and compressive forces act simultaneously?
options: Mortise and tenon with draw-boring
Housed dovetail joint
Tusk tenon joint
Cogged and notched joint

question: When installing a hardwood strip floor using secret nailing, at what approximate angle should the nail be driven through the tongue of each board?
options: 90 degrees to the face of the board
45 degrees through the shoulder of the tongue
30 degrees to the face of the board
60 degrees through the groove side of the board

question: In setting out stairs, the 'pitch line' is defined as which of the following?
options: The line connecting the nosings of each tread
The centreline of the stringer measured vertically
The horizontal line from which riser heights are measured
The line parallel to the wall at the handrail height

question: A plywood sheet is described as 'WBP bonded'. What does this bonding classification primarily indicate about the adhesive used?
options: It is weather and boil proof, suitable for external and structural applications
It is water-based polymer adhesive suitable for interior use only
It is a white bond phenolic adhesive that resists moderate moisture
It indicates the ply veneers are bonded with a waterproof barrier paint

question: When using a router to form a housing joint, climb cutting is generally avoided because it causes which specific hazard?
options: The router bit rotates too slowly reducing cut quality
The workpiece or router can be violently pulled in an uncontrolled direction
The router overheats due to friction on the back face of the cutter
The depth of cut becomes inconsistent due to bit deflection

question: Which of the following best describes the purpose of a 'soldier arch' (flat arch) lintel in traditional brickwork carpentry formwork?
options: To provide a decorative curved profile to window openings
To support brickwork over an opening using voussoirs arranged with vertical joints radiating to a centre point
To form a temporary wooden mould that supports flat brickwork over an opening during construction
To provide a structural steel lintel concealed within the masonry

question: In the fabrication of a geometrical stair with a wreathed handrail, the term 'falling line' refers to which of the following?
options: The vertical line dropped from the centre of the handrail to the pitch line
The line on the face mould that represents the intersection of the rail with the cylinder of the newel
The curved line on the developed surface of the wreath that corresponds to the slope of the handrail
The line indicating the fall of rainwater across the landing

question: When producing setting-out rods for a casement window frame, which dimension is typically deducted from the structural opening width to determine the frame width?
options: 10 mm for tolerances only
The combined thickness of both vertical linings plus a tolerance allowance
The width of the wall reveal on one side
The thickness of external cladding plus a DPC allowance

question: Under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations 2015, at what threshold of construction phase duration does a project become notifiable to the Health and Safety Executive?
options: More than 30 working days with more than 20 workers simultaneously on site, or exceeds 500 person-days
More than 14 working days with any workers on site
More than 60 working days regardless of worker numbers
More than 500 person-days only, with no duration threshold

question: Which defect in timber is described as a localised area where fibres are interlocked and grain direction changes abruptly, significantly reducing the timber's strength in bending?
options: Reaction wood
Interlocked grain
A knot
Case hardening

question: When glazing a hardwood sash window with double-glazed sealed units, which method of securing the glass provides the best long-term performance and weather resistance?
options: Linseed oil putty bedded and front puttied in the traditional manner
Sprung glazing beads secured with lost-head nails and bedded in silicone sealant
Timber beads bradded in place with a dry gasket seal
Lead came and copper wire ties fixed to the glazing bar rebates

question: In advanced sheet material technology, 'MDF with moisture resistant core' (MR MDF) achieves its resistance through which manufacturing modification?
options: The addition of a wax emulsion and moisture-resistant urea-formaldehyde or melamine-urea-formaldehyde resin binder during production
The application of a factory-applied vapour barrier membrane bonded to both faces
The use of softwood fibres only, which are naturally less hygroscopic than hardwood fibres
The pressure impregnation of the finished board with a boron-based preservative solution
